entries.name: <a>
entries.description: Turns text or other content into a clickable link. The href attribute sets where the browser goes when the link is activated.
Displays a picture on the page. Always pair src with alt text so the image still makes sense to screen readers or when it fails to load.

entries.name: <div>
entries.description: A plain block-level box with no meaning of its own. Use it to group related content together for styling or layout.

entries.name: <span>
entries.description: A plain inline wrapper for a small piece of text. Handy when you want to style just a few words inside a sentence.
Marks a paragraph of text. Browsers add spacing between paragraphs so long content stays readable.

entries.name: <h1>
entries.description: The main heading of a page. Each page should normally have just one, with h2 through h6 used for smaller subheadings.

entries.name: <ul>
entries.description: A bulleted list for items where order does not matter. Every entry inside it must be an li element.

entries.name: <ol>
entries.description: A numbered list for steps or rankings where order matters. The browser handles the numbering for you.

entries.name: <li>
entries.description: One item inside a ul or ol list. It can hold text, links, or even a whole nested list.

entries.name: <table>
entries.description: Lays out data in rows and columns. Best for genuinely tabular content like schedules and price grids, not page layout.

entries.name: <form>
entries.description: Wraps a group of inputs so their values can be sent somewhere. The action and method attributes control where and how the data is submitted.

entries.name: <input>
entries.description: A single field the user can fill in. The type attribute switches it between text, email, checkbox, number, and many other modes.

entries.name: <button>
entries.description: A clickable control for triggering an action, such as submitting a form or running a script. Its label goes between the opening and closing tags.

entries.name: <section>
entries.description: Groups one distinct chunk of a page, like a features area or a testimonials block. It usually starts with its own heading.

entries.name: <nav>
entries.description: Holds the main navigation links of a site or page. Marking the menu with nav helps assistive technology find it quickly.

entries.name: display
entries.description: Decides how an element takes up space and how its children are arranged. Common values include block, inline, flex, grid, and none.

entries.name: color
entries.description: Sets the color of the text inside an element. It accepts names, hex codes, rgb(), and hsl() values.

entries.name: background
entries.description: A shorthand for painting the area behind an element. It can combine a color, an image, a gradient, and positioning in one line.

entries.name: margin
entries.description: Adds empty space outside an element, pushing its neighbors away. One value covers all four sides, or you can set each side separately.

entries.name: padding
entries.description: Adds space inside an element, between its border and its content. Great for giving buttons and cards breathing room.

entries.name: border
entries.description: Draws a line around the edge of an element. The shorthand takes a width, a style such as solid or dashed, and a color.

entries.name: font-size
entries.description: Controls how large text renders. Relative units like rem respect user settings, so they usually beat fixed pixels.

entries.name: font-family
entries.description: Picks the typeface for text. List fallbacks after commas so the browser has options if the first font is unavailable.

entries.name: width
entries.description: Sets how wide an element is. It works with fixed units like px or flexible ones like percentages.

entries.name: height
entries.description: Sets how tall an element is. Leave it unset when possible so content can grow naturally without clipping.

entries.name: flex
entries.description: A shorthand on flex items that controls how they grow, shrink, and what size they start from. Setting flex: 1 makes items share leftover space evenly.

entries.name: gap
entries.description: Adds consistent space between items in a flex or grid container. Much cleaner than juggling margins on every child.

entries.name: grid-template-columns
entries.description: Defines the column layout of a grid container. The repeat() function and fr units make even, flexible tracks easy.

entries.name: position
entries.description: Changes how an element is placed in the page flow. Values like relative, absolute, fixed, and sticky unlock offsets through top, right, bottom, and left.

entries.name: border-radius
entries.description: Rounds the corners of an element. Small values soften cards, and a very large value turns a square avatar into a circle.

entries.name: Array.map()
entries.description: Builds a new array by running a function on every item of the original. The source array is left untouched.

entries.name: Array.filter()
entries.description: Returns a new array containing only the items that pass a test function. Items that return false are dropped.

entries.name: Array.forEach()
entries.description: Runs a function once for each item in an array. Use it for side effects like logging, since it does not build a new array.

entries.name: Array.push()
entries.description: Appends one or more values to the end of an array and returns the new length. This changes the original array in place.

entries.name: Array.includes()
entries.description: Checks whether an array contains a specific value and answers with true or false.

entries.name: String.split()
entries.description: Cuts a string into an array of pieces using a separator you choose. Splitting on a comma is a quick way to read simple lists.

entries.name: String.trim()
entries.description: Returns a copy of the string with whitespace removed from both ends. Useful for cleaning up form input before validating it.

entries.name: String.toUpperCase()
entries.description: Returns a new string with every letter converted to capitals. The original string stays the same.

entries.name: JSON.parse()
entries.description: Converts a JSON text string into a live JavaScript value, usually an object or array. It throws an error if the text is not valid JSON.

entries.name: JSON.stringify()
entries.description: Turns a JavaScript value into a JSON string, which is handy for saving to storage or sending to a server.
entries.example: const text = JSON.stringify({ id: 7, done: false });

entries.name: document.querySelector()
entries.description: Finds the first element in the page that matches a CSS selector. It returns null when nothing matches, so check before using the result.

entries.name: addEventListener()
entries.description: Registers a function to run whenever a given event happens on an element, such as a click or a keypress.

entries.name: setTimeout()
entries.description: Schedules a function to run once after a delay measured in milliseconds. It returns an id you can pass to clearTimeout to cancel it.

entries.name: Math.random()
entries.description: Produces a pseudo-random decimal from 0 up to, but not including, 1. Multiply and floor it to get whole numbers in a range.

entries.name: Number.parseInt()
entries.description: Reads a whole number from the start of a string, ignoring trailing text. Always pass 10 as the second argument to force base ten.

entries.name: print()
entries.description: Writes values to the screen, separating multiple arguments with spaces and ending with a newline by default.

entries.name: len()
entries.description: Returns how many items something holds, whether it is a string, list, tuple, or dictionary.

entries.name: range()
entries.description: Generates a sequence of whole numbers, most often used to drive a for loop. The end value is not included.

entries.name: input()
entries.description: Pauses the program and waits for the user to type a line of text. Whatever they enter always comes back as a string.

entries.name: int()
entries.description: Converts a value such as a numeric string or a float into a whole number. Floats are truncated toward zero rather than rounded.

entries.name: str()
entries.description: Converts any value into its text form. Useful when you need to glue numbers into messages.

entries.name: list()
entries.description: Creates a new list, or converts another iterable like a string or a range into one.

entries.name: dict()
entries.description: Creates a dictionary of key and value pairs. You can build one from keyword arguments or from a sequence of pairs.

entries.name: sum()
entries.description: Adds up all the numbers in an iterable and returns the total.

entries.name: sorted()
entries.description: Returns a new sorted list from any iterable, leaving the original untouched. A key function or reverse=True customizes the order.

entries.name: enumerate()
entries.description: Loops over an iterable while also counting, giving you each index and item together. Cleaner than managing a counter by hand.
entries.example:
for i, item in enumerate(["a", "b"]):
    print(i, item)

entries.name: open()
entries.description: Opens a file for reading or writing and returns a file object. Using it inside a with block closes the file automatically.
entries.example:
with open("notes.txt") as f:
    text = f.read()

entries.name: SELECT
entries.description: Reads data out of a table. List the columns you want, or use * to fetch every column.

entries.name: WHERE
entries.description: Filters rows so a query only touches those matching a condition. It works with SELECT, UPDATE, and DELETE.

entries.name: ORDER BY
entries.description: Sorts the rows a query returns by one or more columns. Add DESC to sort from highest to lowest.
entries.example: SELECT * FROM posts ORDER BY created_at DESC;

entries.name: INSERT INTO
entries.description: Adds a new row to a table. Name the columns, then supply a matching value for each one.

entries.name: UPDATE
entries.description: Changes values in existing rows. Always pair it with a WHERE clause, or every row in the table will be modified.
entries.example: UPDATE products SET price = 9.99 WHERE id = 3;

entries.name: DELETE
entries.description: Removes rows from a table. Like UPDATE, it applies to every row unless a WHERE clause narrows it down.
entries.example: DELETE FROM sessions WHERE expired = true;

entries.name: JOIN
entries.description: Combines rows from two tables by matching values, usually a foreign key against a primary key. This lets one query pull related data together.
entries.example:
SELECT o.id, u.name FROM orders o
JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id;

entries.name: GROUP BY
entries.description: Collapses rows that share a value into groups so aggregate functions like COUNT and SUM can summarize each group.
entries.example: SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM tickets GROUP BY status;

entries.name: LIMIT
entries.description: Caps how many rows a query returns. Combine it with ORDER BY to fetch things like the newest twenty records.
entries.example: SELECT * FROM logs ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 20;

entries.name: CREATE TABLE
entries.description: Defines a brand new table, naming each column along with its data type and any constraints.
entries.example:
CREATE TABLE tags (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, label TEXT);

entries.name: git init
entries.description: Turns the current folder into a new Git repository by creating a hidden .git directory. Run it once at the start of a project.

entries.name: git clone
entries.description: Downloads a full copy of a remote repository, including its entire history, into a new local folder.

entries.name: git add
entries.description: Stages changes so they are included in the next commit. You can stage single files or everything at once with a dot.

entries.name: git commit
entries.description: Saves the staged changes as a snapshot in the repository history. The -m flag attaches a short message describing what changed.

entries.name: git status
entries.description: Shows which files are modified, staged, or untracked right now. A quick sanity check before committing.

entries.name: git log
entries.description: Lists past commits, newest first, with their authors and messages. Flags like --oneline condense the output.

entries.name: git branch
entries.description: Lists your branches, or creates a new one when you pass a name. Branches let you build features without touching main.

entries.name: git checkout
entries.description: Switches your working folder to another branch or commit. With the -b flag it creates the branch and switches in one step.

entries.name: git merge
entries.description: Brings the commits from another branch into the current one. Run it from the branch that should receive the changes.
entries.example:
git checkout main
git merge feature/checkout

entries.name: git push
entries.description: Uploads your local commits to a remote repository so others can see them. Name the remote and the branch you are pushing.
